findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty/null and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In EventManager.create(), the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. The `?? []` fallback only handles null/undefined; when destinationCalendar is an empty array (or null), the destructured `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so reading `.integration` throws a TypeError. Many callers updated in this PR now pass `[]` when there is no destination calendar (e.g. confirm.handler, stripe webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, editLocation.handler), and handleNewBooking passes `null`. Any booking on a Google Meet location where the organizer has no destination calendar will now crash during eventManager.create(), failing the booking/confirmation flow. The old code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) and was safe. This needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback computes an undefined calendarId
findings.body: In updateEvent the fallback is `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, the `find` predicate compares each calendar's externalId against that same falsy externalCalendarId, so it can never match — selectedCalendar is always `undefined`. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which actually resolved to the destination calendar. The same broken fallback was copied into deleteEvent (line ~317). Any update/delete where the booking reference has no externalCalendarId (older bookings, or references created without externalId) will now call the Google API with an undefined calendarId, so event updates and deletions silently fail, leaving stale events on users' calendars.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined selectedCalendar instead of the inserted calendar
findings.body: In createEvent, the insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that writes the description with the hangout link uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destinationCalendar entry matches the credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined: the event is created on "primary" but the patch is issued with an undefined calendarId, which the googleapis client rejects (or targets nothing), so the hangout link is never written into the event description. The patch call also has no callback/await, so the failure is an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: updateLocation referencesToCreate loses credentialId and externalCalendarId for calendar results
findings.body: In updateLocation, referencesToCreate now maps `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`. However, calendar results here come from updateAllCalendarEvents -> CalendarManager.updateEvent, whose returned EventResult object never sets `externalId` or `credentialId` (only createEvent in CalendarManager was updated to include them). editLocation.handler then persists these via `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`, creating new booking references with both fields undefined. Downstream, cancel/update flows rely on reference.credentialId and reference.externalCalendarId; losing them forces fallback paths (deleting via every user credential, or the broken undefined-calendarId fallback in the Google service). Previously externalCalendarId was taken from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and was populated.

findings.title: References created for destinations without credentialId get no externalCalendarId
findings.body: In createAllCalendarEvents, when a destinationCalendar entry has no credentialId, the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`. CalendarManager.createEvent only puts the passed externalId onto the returned EventResult, and EventManager.create() now builds references with `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`. So for any DestinationCalendar row whose credentialId is null (the column is nullable), the stored booking reference will have externalCalendarId undefined, and later updates/deletes of that event hit the Google service with a null externalCalendarId — which (combined with the broken fallback there) targets an undefined calendar. The old code always used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` for the reference.

findings.title: Recurring cancel-all deletes duplicate per reference and only delete the first calendar reference of each booking
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch (recurringEvent + allRemainingBookings) lives inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, so with the multiple calendar references this PR introduces (one per collective host), the entire 'delete across all user calendar credentials for all updatedBookings' block executes once per reference, duplicating every deletion API call. Worse, inside that block each updated booking's reference is resolved with `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which only returns the first calendar reference — so the additional hosts' calendar events for recurring collective bookings are never deleted when cancelling all remaining bookings.

findings.title: loadUsers refactor drops organization.slug from the dynamic-user select
findings.body: The rewritten loadUsers for dynamic bookings (no eventTypeId) selects `...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true` but no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which the previous code included. Downstream booking logic (e.g. bookerUrl/organization-aware links) relies on `user.organization.slug`; for dynamic group bookings this will now be undefined, regressing organization bookings.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: The evt is built with `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, and later `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }`. If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar but other collective hosts do, evt.destinationCalendar is null and the optional-chained push is a no-op — the team members' destination calendars are silently discarded and no calendar events are created for any host. It should initialize with `(evt.destinationCalendar ?? [])` before pushing.

findings.title: Webhook payload for destinationCalendar is inconsistent across triggers (null vs [])
findings.body: This test now expects BOOKING_REJECTED payloads to contain `destinationCalendar: []` while the BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED assertions in the same file still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The difference comes from handleNewBooking emitting null when there is no destination calendar while confirm.handler and others emit []. Webhook consumers now see two different shapes for the same field depending on the trigger, which is a needless API inconsistency for a PR described as non-breaking.
